ref_text: The street was quiet before dawn, and everyone waited for the clock to reach five.

lines.text: Sweden once made every driver on the road stop dead at ten to five on a September morning in 1967,
lines.text_kokoro: Sweden once made every driver on the road stop dead at ten to five on a September morning in nineteen sixty-seven,

lines.text: because at five o'clock, the whole country would switch to driving on the right, like its neighbours.
So when they all switched at once, did road deaths go up, or down?
Drivers like Ingrid had driven on the left all their lives, and one slip of habit would put them head-on into someone.
Deaths went down, by almost half, with speed limits cut.
For two months, it looked as if the switch they called Dagen H had made Sweden's roads safer overnight.

lines.text: But by November, with the limits still down, the deaths were back where they'd been, because once the road felt normal, the care wore off.
So the safest Ingrid ever drove was the morning she was sure she'd crash.
